evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper, an S52 manual M Roadster is the preferred engine. Without records or structural evidence, however, this example does not demonstrate the superiority needed to justify keeper money during the current cash-preservation phase.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a manual M Roadster with a hardtop in straight-looking silver paint and a black interior with moderate wear. The 1998 model year implies the S52, but there is no VIN to confirm identity, title or history. Two things are observed in the photos: an illuminated CHECK ENGINE lamp in the odometer shot, and blue-green coolant residue on an aged expansion tank. The odometer photo also reads 69,351 against the stated 69,532. The car carries lowering suspension, aftermarket camber plates and a Dinan strut bar. The 'brand new H&R ($1,900)' claim has no receipt. The two model-critical items that apply, rear-structure condition and cooling history, are entirely missing, which matters more on a Midwest car. At $19,950 it sits above the $18,643 fair-value midpoint and has been listed unchanged for months.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a title photo, a running cold-start video showing whether the CEL clears, trunk-floor and underside photos, and confirmation that a PPI at a Milwaukee-area BMW independent is allowed before payment.
